messages:
alex: :rotating_light: Observed surge of authz failures for service-account svc-ingest-prod across three regions. KMS decrypt count jumped ~4x in last 10m. Opening ops room now.

maria: copying. can someone grab audit logs and identity of callers?

jamal: i'm on it, pulling CloudAudit. running quick query -> `resource.name:projects/*/serviceAccounts/svc-ingest-prod AND protoPayload.methodName: "google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"`

nina: sec-bot flagged repeated short-lived tokens for that SA, looks like ephemeral creds were minted from CI pipeline. saving evidence.

sec-bot: automated-detection: alert_id=KMS-DECRYPT-SPIKE-1999, severity=high, correlated_events=78, rule=service_account_decrypt_spike_v2

henry: assign roles: jamal SRE lead for containment, maria sec lead, nina evidence collection, i'll notify product owner and freeze deploys for ingest.

alex: jamal, required containment options: 1) disable SA keys, 2) rotate KMS key, 3) narrow RBAC by removing iam.serviceAccounts.actAs temporarily. prefer 1+3 to maintain data availability.

jamal: i can remove the actAs binding from the CI runner role now, that'll block new impersonations. executing: `gcloud iam roles remove-iam-policy-binding --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`

maria: collect timeline: first anomalous decrypt 1999998920, spike from 1999998940-1999998980, origin IPs include 52.14.23.7, 18.205.102.44, and internal runner pool. saving to incident doc.

nina: copied logs to /incidents/1999999000/evidence/raw-logs.json and uploaded to secure bucket. note: log shows repeated decrypts for smaller ciphertext blobs — looks like someone exfiltrating key-encrypted material.

henry: decided: do NOT rotate primary KMS key yet (would break in-flight jobs). instead revoke the specific SA keys and create short-term service account token freeze. maria, confirm we can revoke SA tokens via IAM sessions API.

maria: yes, we can revoke tokens by disabling the SA's keys and setting iam.policy condition to block token minting. i'll put the conditional deny in place now.

jamal: containment step 1 done: removed actAs binding from CI runner role. step 2 in progress: disabling SA user-managed keys (2 key ids found).

sec-bot: system: deployment pipeline triggered rollback of last two ingest jobs as precaution.

alex: heads-up: we need to preserve audit logs for compliance. nina, ensure retention copied to long-term archive and lock writes.

nina: copying to compliant-retention bucket with immutability tag, done.

maria: we should rotate any tokens that were minted in the window. making a list of affected tokens and owners. will notify identity provider for emergency rotation.

henry: comms: drafting customer-facing note in #announcements-draft. internal postmortem template created at /incidents/1999999000/postmortem.md.

alex: next: evidence collection complete? if so we can handoff to night ops team in 30m. include playbook steps for them.

nina: evidence collection complete. attached timeline and hashes in the incident doc.

jamal: containment verified: decrypt rate down to baseline, no new impersonation attempts in last 8m. keeping monitoring on 1m alerts.

maria: sec follow-ups: 1) audit RBAC policies across CI runners, 2) implement time-bound actAs for build jobs, 3) add alerting for KMS request patterns. logging ticket created: #INC-1999999.

henry: handoff to night ops in 30: @oncall-night please pick up monitoring and run through checklist in incident doc. i'll hand off with a short call at 1999999120.

alex: thanks team — good containment. leaving room open for final notes.

sec-bot: system: incident state -> contained; severity -> mitigated; watchers updated.
